app_documentation:
Simple Task Manager is a web-based personal task management application that lets individual users record, track, and clean up the work they need to do. It is built as a React front end backed by a Node.js and Express REST API, with PostgreSQL as the database. The main purpose is to give users one fast loop: add a task, check it off, filter the list, and delete tasks they no longer need. A new user should be able to create and complete a task within one minute without instructions.

The application delivers four core features. Create Task (F1, High priority) lets a user add a task with a required title and an optional description. An empty title shows a validation error and no task is created. Complete Task (F2, High) lets a user mark a task complete or revert it to incomplete, and the status persists after reload. Delete Task (F3, High) permanently removes a task only after the user confirms in a dialog. Cancelling leaves the task unchanged. View Task List (F4, Medium) shows all of a user's tasks with title and status, and supports filtering by All, Active, and Completed.

The user experience is a card-based, mobile-first design with an indigo primary color and Inter typography. It has five screens: Task List, New Task, Task Details, Delete Confirmation, and Empty State. Supporting elements include status badges, toasts (success on add, and an undo toast on status change), a character counter on the title field, and a floating add button. Accessibility targets WCAG AA contrast, 44px touch targets, visible focus rings, aria-live error announcements, and full keyboard support. On tablet and desktop the content is centered in a 720px column.

The intended audience is a single role, User: any individual who wants a simple personal to-do list. The data model has a users table and a tasks table. Each task belongs to exactly one user and is deleted with a hard delete. Tasks carry a required non-empty title, an optional description, an is_completed flag, and a completed_at timestamp. Non-functional requirements are: task list pages load in under 2 seconds at 100 concurrent users, at least 99.5% monthly uptime, all traffic over HTTPS, and strict per-user data isolation, so every API query is filtered by the authenticated user. Delivery follows the 12-task MVP plan (T1-T12), covering schema, API, UI, accessibility polish, and end-to-end, load, and uptime verification. Known risks to track are the unspecified authentication scope, a late schema change risk, over-building of design-only elements, hosting and performance targets, and accidental data loss from the permanent delete flow. Two discrepancies to resolve are that the plan states a title max of 100 characters while the schema allows varchar(255), and that the plan's schema task names a 'completed' column while the approved schema uses is_completed.

glossary.Task: A single to-do item owned by one user, with a required title, an optional description, and a completion status (incomplete or complete).
glossary.Complete / Incomplete Status: The state of a task stored as the boolean is_completed, with completed_at recording when it was completed. Users can toggle it in either direction, and the change persists after reload.
glossary.Task Filter: A control on the Task List (All, Active, Completed) that limits the displayed tasks by completion status.
glossary.Hard Delete: Permanent removal of a task from the list and the database after user confirmation, with no soft-delete or recovery.
glossary.User-Scoped Access: The security rule that each user can see and change only their own tasks. The API enforces it by filtering all queries by the authenticated user_id, over HTTPS.
glossary.Baseline: An approved, versioned snapshot of a project artifact (such as Requirements_v1 or Design_v1) that serves as the reference point for change control and support.
